claims.statement: Polish network companies reported 7,817 refusals of electricity-grid connection conditions in 2024 covering 73,586.12 MW; 4,443 were attributed to lack of technical conditions and 2,196 to economic conditions.

The high refusal count makes pre-application capital preservation and redesign a plausible paid event for smaller developers, although the aggregate contains heterogeneous projects and does not prove prediction is possible from public data.
It is unknown whether accessible DSO information is sufficiently granular to outperform experienced local engineering firms on connection outcomes.

contrary_evidence: URE's count is an aggregate of applications and may include duplicate, speculative, or utility-scale requests outside the proposed customer segment.
DSOs retain decision authority and important network constraints may be unavailable or change after the screen.
Experienced grid consultants already sell application support, and long project cycles delay learning and cash conversion.

economics.acquisition_route: Embed the paid readiness check into renewable-land listings and EPC proposal software before a parcel is represented as connection-ready; land brokers and EPCs earn a disclosed referral share and avoid wasting engineering time on obviously weak sites. Publish DSO-specific application checklists to capture high-intent search demand.
economics.founder_time: Part-time validation hypothesis; delivery burden remains untested.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: The combination of DSO-specific submission playbooks, observed application outcomes, standardized techno-economic redesign models, and a licensed-engineer review queue makes each screen faster and more consistent. Outcome data improve the workflow but are not claimed as a standalone moat.
fingerprint.customer: Polish small renewable and storage developers, commercial-rooftop EPCs, landowners, and project financiers evaluating roughly sub-utility-scale sites before a grid application or after a refusal.
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Embed the paid readiness check into renewable-land listings and EPC proposal software before a parcel is represented as connection-ready; land brokers and EPCs earn a disclosed referral share and avoid wasting engineering time on obviously weak sites. Publish DSO-specific application checklists to capture high-intent search demand.
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Combine public network plans and refusal patterns, site/load data, generation simulations, application completeness checks, and licensed electrical-engineer review into a bankable red/amber/green memo. For failed sites, model capped export, storage, demand co-location, or revised capacity and coordinate the resubmission. Sell per-site reports plus portfolio subscriptions to EPCs and financiers.
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The developer pays per site for a pre-application risk screen and documentation data room, then a larger fixed fee when commissioning a licensed-engineer redesign or refusal-response package; payment is tied to completed deliverables, not a promise of connection.
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A land option, equipment deposit, financing decision, connection application, or DSO refusal forces the buyer to decide whether to proceed, resize, add storage, change export limits, or abandon the site.

founder_fit: Strong quantitative fit: spatial data, scenario modelling, automation, and renewable-energy domain access.
Can begin as a narrow analysis desk alongside employment without financing or owning projects.
Requires credentialed engineering review and clear separation between analytical pre-screening and formal grid design.
risks: Evidence of a workflow, transition, or loss does not yet establish recurring willingness to pay.
The proposed distribution and compounding mechanisms remain hypotheses pending buyer evidence.

title: Grid-Connection Readiness and Hybrid Redesign Desk
uncertainties: Number of addressable sub-utility projects and their current spend on failed applications.
Predictive value of public plans, historical refusals, nearby loads, and substation data at site level.
Professional liability and the licensed-engineer cost per reviewed report.
Pricing, buyer authority, and acquisition economics remain unvalidated at discovery.

First validation test: Obtain 20 historical application files with known outcomes from at least three developers or EPCs, make blinded risk predictions from information available at filing time, and measure discrimination. Then sell five fixed-fee live screens; stop if predictions do not beat a simple DSO/region baseline or no buyer pays before the application.
